title: Telemetry-driven circuit orchestration for stateful streaming
creator: Marcus Liu
description: Implement a telemetry-first circuit orchestration layer for the hosted API edge that gracefully sheds load and rebinds stateful streaming sessions during cross-region capacity pressure. Goal: maintain SLOs for tail latency and availability by coordinating per-request circuit decisions, session rebind attempts, and staged traffic shifts without user-visible stream truncation when possible.
acceptance_criteria: Edge gateway emits per-route circuit state and metrics (open/half-open/closed) and corresponding sample traces to tracing-dash
Automated load-shedding policy shuts off non-essential routes and downgraded model variants under defined capacity signatures within 200ms of detection
Streaming sessions (server-sent events and WebSocket proxied token streams) support transparent rebind protocol: client reconnect hint + server-side buffered prefix resume for <= 60s KV cache age
Cross-region rebinds preserve session affinity for pinned sessions where possible and gracefully degrade to stateless fallback with explicit user-visible code 429/503 when not
Runbook validated in staged canary: circuit trip simulated in us-east-1 and traffic partially shifted to eu-west-1 with <1% increase in 99th-percentile latency for pinned sessions
Playbook includes automated rollback criteria and postmortem checklist when customer-facing errors exceed threshold
telemetry_signatures: Sustained GPU utilization > 85% across region pool for 30s
Token-generation tail latency (99th) increases by > 2x relative to baseline for a model-route pair
Error rate (5xx) for streaming routes > 1% sustained over 60s
KV cache miss storm: miss rate jumps > 10 percentage points coincident with latency spike
rollout_plan: Phase 0: feature-flag behind canary rollout to 3% of traffic in us-east-1
Phase 1: extend to 20% with metric guards (SLOs and errors), enable limited rebind for non-pinned sessions
Phase 2: enable full telemetry-driven shedding and cross-region rebinds for pinned sessions; monitor for 48h
Phase 3: global enable with automated fallback to stateless endpoints and customer notifications
mitigation_playbook: If 5xx > 2% after rollout: immediately flip canary flag to off and scale up dedicated pool by +20%
If reconnect resume fails for > 0.5% of sessions: trigger quick rollback and create incident with SRE
Emergency: force circuit to open for affected route and route to cheaper, non-streaming fallback models with user-visible guidance
Post-incident: run full postmortem, include sampling of problematic traces and KV cache contents where permitted

risk_assessment: Medium-High: incorrect rebind handling can cause user-visible stream truncation or duplicate outputs
Operational complexity: telemetry noise and false positives could trigger unnecessary shedding; mitigated via multi-signal gating and short dampening windows
Compliance risk: storing streamed prefixes for resume touches customer data; limited to <60s buffer and encrypted at rest per KMS policy
rollback_criteria: Customer-facing error rate increases > 0.5% relative to baseline after canary expansion
99th-percentile latency for pinned sessions increases by > 20% sustained for 15m
Critical telemetry pipeline lag exceeds 30s causing stale circuit decisions
